It is a fine-tune of Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct on xlam-function-calling-60k plus xlam-irrelevance-7.5k, using function masking (arXiv 2410.04587). Its calls are JSON {name, arguments}, wrapped in ``` fences per the card example. The card's June 2025 note says it was integrated into Google AI Edge; search results tie this to the AI Edge Function Calling SDK (MediaPipe), not GGUF. models_verified.notes: Verified. Created 2026-07-02. The GitHub repo Tahleels/json-extract-qlora-dpo exists. The recipe matches the candidate description: Faker with 14 templates; SFT 3,400 train / 200 val / 400 test; 2,000 DPO pairs with rejected outputs corrupted by fences, preambles, trailing commas, single quotes and missing fields; QLoRA r=16 / alpha 32 on all attention and MLP projections, 3 epochs, lr 2e-4; DPO beta 0.1, 1 epoch, lr 5e-6. Main value: the DPO-on-format-corruptions step is a cheap recipe to copy onto LFM2.5-350M. With a JSON-schema grammar at inference, though, much of what that step fixes (fences, preambles) is already blocked. Source: https://huggingface.co/tahleels/qwen2.5-0.5b-json-extraction-qlora-dpo

models_verified.notes:
Repo created 2026-09-16 and last updated 2026-10-02, so it is still changing. total_parameters = 121,021,910, most of it in the engram table. On Cactus's own extraction benchmarks (SNIPS) it trails LFM2.5-350M, the current best in the ladder, so it is not a clear quality win. Its strength is size: 35 MB.

Extraction API: you pass a Pydantic or JSON schema (enums via Literal, arrays and nested objects allowed). The grammar forces keys and braces, and the docs say "a field is filled only from a span of the passage". That span-grounding could be a problem for JobTrail fields that need inference rather than copying: laborMinutes from '2 hrs', the customerApproved boolean, the jobType enum. This is unverified.

Context: 8,192 tokens, with an int8 KV cache post-trained at a 256 window. Docs warn accuracy falls as the prefix grows past about two dozen tools.

Fine-tuning: LoRA on the attention projections in JAX (CPU, CUDA or Metal). `needle build --layers N` merges the adapter and exports a 4-bit .cact. The 2-bit post-training behind the shipped 35 MB file runs only on the paid Cactus Platform, so a self-fine-tuned model would be 4-bit and larger (size unverified).

Adopting it means a second runtime alongside llama.rn and wllama. Older siblings: Cactus-Compute/needle2 (45M, 2026-07-29) and needle (2026-03-16, MIT, JAX).

Parameter count: 361.8M is computed from config.json (tied embeddings). The GGUF stores an untied output matrix, giving 409.0M params. That matches the GGUF metadata exactly and explains why the Q4_K_M is 303.0 MB. There is no Q8_0; the F16 is 819.9 MB.

runtime_claim_checks.claim: llama.cpp's JSON-schema-to-GBNF converter supports minimum/exclusiveMinimum only for integer, not number, and skips unsupported features silently. So schema.v2 materials[].quantity {type:number, exclusiveMinimum:0} is not enforced while decoding. laborMinutes (integer 0..1440) is enforced.
runtime_claim_checks.evidence:
I tried to refute the claim and couldn't. The docs, the current source code, the llama.cpp version bundled in wllama, and our own eval runs all support it.

1. Docs. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/grammars/README.md (fetched 2026-10-02). Its limitations list says the four bounds keywords (minimum, exclusiveMinimum, maximum, exclusiveMaximum) are "only supported for "type": "integer" for now, not number". The same list says "Unsupported features are skipped silently". The README also has a worked Zod example: age = z.number().positive() becomes {"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0}. The grammar it generates is `age-kv ::= "\"age\"" space ":" space number`, with no lower bound. That is the same shape as our materials[].quantity.

2. Current master source, after the refactor in PR #28736 (merged 2026-09-03), which moved schema parsing into common/json-schema.cpp:
   - https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/common/json-schema.cpp: build_integer() reads minimum, exclusiveMinimum (+1), maximum and exclusiveMaximum (-1). For "number", build_node() returns a bare common_chat_schema_number with no bound fields and no warning.
   - https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/common/json-schema.h: common_chat_schema_number has no members. common_chat_schema_integer has inclusive int64 minimum and maximum.
   - https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp: KIND_NUMBER emits the plain number primitive. KIND_INTEGER emits build_min_max_int(min, max). The only warning in the converter is for unsupported regex patterns, so dropped number bounds produce no message.
   - https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tests/test-json-schema.cpp: a test parses {"type":"number","minimum":1,"maximum":2} into a plain common_chat_schema_number. Another test folds integer exclusiveMinimum 0 into minimum 1.

3. The llama.cpp commit vendored by wllama 3.6.1 (the version in apps/web/package.json) is 83d855c5, dated 2026-08-27, from before the refactor. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/83d855c5a6d70487121edbf4020b25c96b7a04e7/common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp only applies the bounds when schema_type == "integer". It has the comment "TODO: support minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum at least for zero" before falling back to the plain number primitive. wllama 3.6.1 builds llama.cpp/common/*.cpp and includes server-context.h and server-schema.h (https://github.com/ngxson/wllama/blob/3.6.1/cpp/wllama-context.h, https://github.com/ngxson/wllama/blob/3.6.1/CMakeLists.txt). So response_format json_schema in the browser goes through the same converter. I found no LLGuidance in the wllama build.

5. laborMinutes. The local packages/core/schema/schema.v2.json has anyOf[{type:integer, minimum:0, maximum:1440}, {type:null}]. The integer branch becomes build_min_max_int(0, 1440), so it is enforced while decoding. quantity is anyOf[{type:number, exclusiveMinimum:0}, {type:null}], and its number branch has no bound.

Caveats (these refine the claim; they don't refute it):
- Builds compiled with -DLLAMA_LLGUIDANCE=ON (off by default, needs Rust) send JSON schemas to LLGuidance instead (json_schema_to_grammar returns "%llguidance ..."). https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/llguidance.md says "no keywords are silently ignored" there. https://github.com/guidance-ai/llguidance/blob/main/docs/json_schema.md lists the four bounds keywords as supported for both integer and number.
- The README's advice to use the Python converter to see warnings is out of date. examples/json_schema_to_grammar.py returns 404 on master and doesn't appear in the repo tree.
- llama.rn is only planned and I didn't check its source. That it behaves the same (because it vendors llama.cpp common/) is UNVERIFIED.
runtime_claim_checks.corrected: The claim is accurate, with these refinements. In llama.cpp's built-in JSON-schema-to-GBNF converter (common/json-schema.cpp + common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp on master as of 2026-10-02, and the older code in the commit wllama 3.6.1 bundles, 83d855c from 2026-08-27), the four bounds keywords only work for "type":"integer". For "type":"number" they are dropped without any warning. So in schema.v2, materials[].quantity {type:number, exclusiveMinimum:0} is not enforced while decoding: the grammar allows 0, negative numbers and exponent forms. Our runs have already produced quantity 0 (evidence/67, evidence/72). laborMinutes {type:integer, minimum:0, maximum:1440} is enforced by an integer-range grammar rule. The one exception is a llama.cpp build with -DLLAMA_LLGUIDANCE=ON (off by default, needs Rust): it hands schemas to LLGuidance, which supports number bounds and reports unsupported keywords as errors instead of skipping them. That llama.rn behaves the same is unverified. Output must still be re-validated with Zod (packages/core/src/schema.ts already has quantity: z.number().positive().nullable()). Another option is to change the schema so quantity can be enforced in the grammar, for example with a pattern or a different number representation.
